Scaling inference-at-deployment reduces the number of simultaneously served copies of each new model. For example, if inference-at-deployment is scaled by two orders of magnitude, the number of copies can decrease by a factor of 100. This reduction is significant as it affects the immediate impact of the model upon deployment.

Additionally, scaling inference-at-deployment reduces the value of securing model weights. If training compute plateaus while inference-at-deployment scales significantly, the value of stealing model weights does not increase over time, as the costs associated with inference-at-deployment become the primary concern. Even if model weights were stolen, the high costs of inference-at-deployment would still need to be paid, making the weights less valuable.
